changes.before: A hungering bio-swarm. No shields at all, but their flesh knits back together every round.
changes.after: A living weapon that ate its makers. No shields at all, but their flesh knits back together every round.

changes.before: Pirate raiders in stolen hulls. Fast, thin shields, and far too many torpedoes.
changes.after: Furred pack hunters in ships that run dark, stripping every wreck. Fast, thin shields, and far too many rockets.

changes.before: Machine necropolis-ships. Gauss weapons tear through shields, and wrecks sometimes stand back up.
changes.after: Starwright minds in machine bodies, stealing starlight to light a new sun. Null weapons cut through shields and armor, and wrecks rebuild themselves.

changes.before: An imperial war-machine of wedge-hulled destroyers. Ion cannons strip shields; carriers launch fighter screens.
changes.after: The Registry’s navy: linked crews, wedge hulls and drone escorts. Ion cannons strip shields; carriers launch fighter screens.

changes.before: An ancient, dying elder race. Blindingly fast, heavily shielded, fragile once the shields fall.
changes.after: Few, long-lived masters of light and crystal. Blindingly fast, heavily shielded, fragile once the shields fall.

changes.before: Gothic crusader battleships. Heavy armor, lance batteries and broadsides that hit like a cathedral falling.
changes.after: The frontier the Hegemony wrote off, come to stop the Siphoning. Black-iron battleships: heavy armor, lances, and broadsides that hit harder on the move.

changes.before: Corsairs field no lance weapons (no long-range beams): they win up close.
changes.after: Hullbreakers field no lance weapons (no long-range beams): they win up close.

changes.before: Ithar hulls cannot Brace for impact: they live by shields and speed.
changes.after: Glasswright hulls cannot Brace for impact: they live by shields and speed.

changes.before: When an enemy ship dies, the Chorus ship that killed it regrows 12% of its hull and every other Chorus ship within 2 hexes regrows 6%, up to 15% per ship each round.
changes.after: When an enemy ship dies, the Chorus ship that killed it regrows 12% of its hull and every other Chorus ship within 2 hexes regrows 6%, up to 12% per ship each round.

changes.before: Corsairs field no lance weapons, and their rocket pods fire salvos that point defense can thin.
changes.after: Hullbreakers field no lance weapons, and their rocket pods fire salvos that point defense can thin.

changes.before: The first Deathless ship to fall each battle (never the flagship) reassembles at the start of the next round with 35% hull and cannot fire that round; a fleet of 6 or more gets two returns. Funeral Pyre stops it.
changes.after: The first Eclipse ship to fall each battle (never the flagship) reassembles at the start of the next round with 35% hull and cannot fire that round; a fleet of 6 or more gets two returns. Funeral Pyre stops it.

changes.before: At the start of its turn, a shield facing that was not hit since its last turn recharges to full, and a facing that was hit recharges twice. Ithar hulls cannot Brace.
changes.after: At the start of its turn, a shield facing that was not hit since its last turn recharges to full, and a facing that was hit recharges twice. Glasswright hulls cannot Brace.

changes.before: Next battle, the endless legion has one more return.
changes.after: Next battle, Archive restore brings back one more ship.

changes.before: free once a tomb-world has woken for you
changes.after: free once a dormant yard has woken a hull for you

changes.before: free once you have joined the song
changes.after: free once you have answered the tone

changes.before: free after an offering at a void-shrine
changes.after: free after an offering at a wall of names

before.d: Their boons are rare more often.
If they watch your run, you start with one of their boons.

after.d: Its protocols are rare more often.
If it is in range of your run, you start with one of its protocols.

changes.before: Its doom arc sits on a turret: it no longer has to turn to fire.
changes.after: Its corona arc sits on a turret: it no longer has to turn to fire.

changes.before: Adds gauss sentries: shoots down squadrons and boarders’ craft.
changes.after: Adds a null spire: shoots down squadrons and boarders’ craft.

changes.before: No hangar; a third turbolaser turret instead.
changes.after: No hangar; a third plasma lance turret instead.

changes.before: A pulsar lance in place of the shuriken cannon.
changes.after: A prism lance in place of the prism shards.

changes.before: Swaps the prow lance for a dorsal macro battery: guns in every arc.
changes.after: Swaps the prow lance for a dorsal sear battery: guns in every arc.

changes.before: torn apart by the dead star
changes.after: torn apart by the Hollow Sun

changes.before: Begin each run with a random relic.
changes.after: Begin each run with a random piece of salvage.

changes.before: Voidsworn fleets may take one Ascendant-class dreadnought.
changes.after: Sunward Crusade fleets may take one Daybreak-class dreadnought.

changes.before: After moving 2+ hexes, enemies get −14 to hit it (others need 3 hexes for −5).
changes.after: After moving 2+ hexes, enemies get −18 to hit it (others need 3 hexes for −5).

changes.before: Port and starboard guns hit 30% harder after moving 2+ hexes (others get 10%).
changes.after: Port and starboard guns hit 40% harder after moving 2+ hexes (others get 10%).

changes.before: Tougher enemies with veteran captains. Drops a relic.
changes.after: Tougher enemies with veteran captains. Drops salvage.

changes.before: Sing, and let the void burn with you.
changes.after: Burn, and let the dark burn with you.

changes.before: A boon is a bonus from a patron that lasts for the rest of this run. Rarity sets how strong it is.
changes.after: A protocol is a bonus from a core that lasts for the rest of this run. Rarity sets how strong it is.

changes.before: A relic is a fleet-wide effect that lasts for the rest of this run.
